title: enhanced-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback: multi-metric matching, staged warmup, and safety guards
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: hardening the unified rollouts controller to reduce false-positives and customer impact during canary/A-B/shadow deployments. This PR implements multi-metric matching, staged warmup windows, and additional safety guards for automated rollback so rollouts are both sensitive to real regressions and resilient to transient noise. Changes include a spec extension for weighted canaries, metric matching profiles, per-stage observation windows, and a conservative fallback policy that pins traffic when thresholds are ambiguous. The description below summarizes intent, design, and rollout plan.  Design highlights: 1) Multi-metric matching - allow rollout policies to evaluate a weighted set of metrics (latency P95, error-rate, token cost divergence, and model quality evals) with configurable thresholds and aggregation strategies. 2) Stage warmup + stabilization windows - each canary stage now supports an independent warmup window where we ignore synthetic spikes and build a baseline for KV-cache/warmup effects. 3) Metric matching profiles - profiles allow teams to declare which metrics matter for a given workload (e.g. latency-first vs quality-first) and provide sane defaults tuned for hosted vs dedicated environments. 4) Conservative fallback and safe-pin - when metric signals are conflicting or insufficient the controller will reduce rollout velocity and eventually pin to the last known-good variant rather than completing the rollout. 5) Observability additions - rollout-delta histograms, per-metric drift alerts, and a "rollout-health" top-level dashboard. 6) E2E and chaos tests - added end-to-end tests that simulate KV-cache warmups and regional capacity changes, plus chaos tests that inject transient downstream errors to validate stability guards.  Migration notes: new policy fields are opt-in; default controller behavior is unchanged unless a new policy is supplied. Backwards compatibility preserved for existing rollout manifests. Deployment plan: staged deploy to staging, canary main cluster, then gradual rollout to hosted; fallback manual gate for enterprise private installs for first 2 weeks. See release notes and usage examples below.

docs: rollout policy examples and migration guide
changes_summary: Added RolloutPolicy.v2 with metricProfiles and stageConfig
Implemented multi-metric evaluator with weighted scoring and tie-break rules
Introduced warmup/stabilization windows to ignore cold-start effects
Implemented conservative fallback that pins previous variant on ambiguous signals
Added rollout-health dashboard and new Prometheus metrics (rollout_delta, rollout_stage_latency_drift)
Added 9 new e2e tests and 4 chaos scenarios
Updated docs and examples for rollout policy migration
review_conversation: Ravi: Overall looks good, a few nits on the evaluator tie-break rules and unit test coverage
Maya: addressed tie-break comments, added explicit doc examples and unit tests for tie scenarios
Lena: can we add a short-circuit for infra errors so we don't trigger quality rollback? Suggest adding 'infrastructure_health' as a gating metric
Maya: added infra gating and updated e2e chaos scenario to validate it
Arjun: approved after verifying the staging run and CI results
Ravi: approval given; recommending a gradual rollout with a monitoring checklist
e2e_run_notes: Staging cluster: simulated KV warmup showed 2-stage stabilization needed for small models
Chaos scenarios: simulated downstream 503 spikes did not trigger rollback due to infra gating metric
Observed metric drift: latency P95 normalized after stage 2 warmup
release_notes: Rollouts: add multi-metric matching and per-stage warmup windows. New RolloutPolicy.v2 is opt-in and backwards compatible. Adds conservative fallback/pin to minimize blast radius on ambiguous signals. Includes new rollout-health dashboard. See docs/rollouts/migration.md for upgrade instructions.
usage_examples: examples/rollouts/weighted_canary.yaml - shows a weighted canary with latency-first metricProfile
docs/rollouts/migration.md - migration guide and new schema reference
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfiguration could cause overly conservative rollouts. Mitigation: defaults are conservative and policy is opt-in
Risk: metric noise causing false positives. Mitigation: staged warmup windows and multi-metric aggregation reduce sensitivity
Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: preconfigured alert thresholds and dashboard guidance included
manual_steps_for_release: Rollout controller: deploy binary to staging, monitor rollout-health dashboard for 24h
Feature flag: enable policy.v2 rolling over a single test service
After 48h of clean metrics, enable for 10% of hosted traffic using weighted canary
After 1 week, consider increasing to 50% with monitoring and manual checkpoints
notes: This PR is intentionally large: it touches controller, evaluator, observability, and tests. We validated behavior in staging over a 72h soak and ran chaos scenarios. Policy.v2 is opt-in; no existing rollouts will change behavior until the new schema is used.
